items.question: Which of these is a gas at room temperature?
items.explanation: Matter is found as solid, liquid or gas. At room temperature, iron and salt are solids, water is a liquid, and oxygen is a gas. We breathe oxygen from the air.

items.question: Ice melting into water is a chemical change.
items.explanation: Melting is a physical change: the ice only changes shape and state, and no new substance is made. You can freeze the water back into ice. A chemical change, like burning paper, makes something new.

items.question: Wet clothes dry in the sun. Which process turns the water in them into a gas?
items.explanation: Evaporation is when a liquid slowly turns into a gas (vapour). Sun, wind and heat make it faster. That is why clothes dry quicker on a hot, windy day.

items.question: The chemical formula of water is ___.
items.explanation: Each water molecule has 2 hydrogen atoms (H) and 1 oxygen atom (O). So we write it H₂O. A single drop of water has billions and billions of these molecules.

items.question: Naphthalene balls kept in a cupboard slowly get smaller but never become liquid. What is this called?
items.explanation: Sublimation is when a solid turns straight into a gas without becoming a liquid first. Naphthalene and camphor both do this. That is why their smell spreads through the cupboard.
